# Redis configured-target reuse audit

## Conclusion

**One definite violation was found.** PR
[#20075](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20075)
reconstructs the configured target for a direct Rediscala client on every stable-semconv command
and transaction execution. No definite violation was found on current `main` or in the other open
Redis-related PR heads.

The audit used `main` at `60a019e5e2d23f87cd8d1272c755ede618e799e8` and PR state observed on
2026-09-14.

## Definite violations

| Location | PR/main | Construction site | Repeated execution path | Stable source/carrier | Recommended capture/reuse point | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`RediscalaServerTargets.java:111–121,145–148`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/faba43d96123befb02625b2faa3a7efb7b04d8ae/instrumentation/rediscala-1.8/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/rediscala/v1_8/RediscalaServerTargets.java#L111-L148) | [#20075](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20075), introduced by the PR | `get()` sends every `RedisClientActorLike` to `of(client)`, which calls `RedisServerTarget.ofHostAndPort(actorClient.host(), actorClient.port())`. This renders an endpoint, parses it, and builds a new target. | Every stable command calls `get(action)` before span creation in [`RequestInstrumentation.java:83–91`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/faba43d96123befb02625b2faa3a7efb7b04d8ae/instrumentation/rediscala-1.8/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/rediscala/v1_8/RequestInstrumentation.java#L83-L91); every stable transaction `exec()` calls it in [`TransactionInstrumentation.java:55–66`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/faba43d96123befb02625b2faa3a7efb7b04d8ae/instrumentation/rediscala-1.8/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/rediscala/v1_8/TransactionInstrumentation.java#L55-L66). These are two consumers of the same construction defect, not separate findings. | The long-lived `RedisClientActorLike`; its configured `host()` and `port()` remain stable between calls to its public `reconnect(String, int)`. The existing [`REQUEST_TARGET`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/faba43d96123befb02625b2faa3a7efb7b04d8ae/instrumentation/rediscala-1.8/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/rediscala/v1_8/RediscalaSingletons.java#L29-L34) demonstrates the intended per-carrier cache. | Retain a target on the actor client, either through a dedicated `VirtualField<RedisClientActorLike, RedisServerTarget>` or the applicable existing request field. Populate lazily or after construction, and refresh/clear it only after successful `reconnect(String, int)`. | High |

This is configured/logical target data, not the selected network peer. The direct actor's
configuration is available on the same durable client before commands execute, and reconstruction
is safe to avoid until `reconnect` changes that configuration. The repeated construction was added
by #20075 (commit
[`a1ff6055`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/a1ff6055c667d70096a493a6d568270e897beeec));
the command and transaction execution paths themselves pre-existed.

## Audited but compliant patterns

### Current `main`

Production code on `main` has the shared
[`RedisServerTarget`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/60a019e5e2d23f87cd8d1272c755ede618e799e8/instrumentation-api-incubator/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/semconv/db/internal/RedisServerTarget.java)
factory but no production instrumentation consumer yet. All Redis families were searched: Jedis
1.4/2.0/3.0/4.0, Lettuce 4.0/5.0/5.1/common, Rediscala 1.8, Redisson
3.0/3.17/common/metrics, and Vert.x Redis client 4.0. Consequently there is no configured-target
construction path on `main` that can violate the reuse rule. Existing connection-address reads in
those modules are not equivalent evidence of repeated configured-`RedisServerTarget` construction.

### Open PR families

- **Redisson #20070:** mutable `Config` is converted during
  `MasterSlaveConnectionManager` construction, retained on the manager, copied by reference to each
  `RedisClient`, and read by requests. The 3.0 and 3.17 configuration adapters perform endpoint
  normalization only at manager initialization.
- **Jedis #20071, #20073, #20074, and #20078:** configured targets are retained on version-appropriate
  long-lived connections, pools, factories, providers, socket factories, cluster handlers, or
  topology state. Command requests copy an existing immutable target reference. Host/port setters,
  Sentinel failover, and slot-cache/topology initialization reconstruct only when configuration or
  topology changes.
- **Lettuce #20072 and #20077:** standalone targets are captured while connections are established;
  cluster seed targets are captured on the cluster client; master/replica iterables are snapshotted
  at `connect`. Connections, endpoints, commands, batch state, callbacks, and reactive subscriptions
  propagate the existing target reference rather than call a target factory.
- **Vert.x #20076 and #20082:** options are converted when the connection manager is constructed.
  The target is retained on the manager and associated with the created `RedisURI`/provider. Request
  objects snapshot that same reference. The 4.4.5 constant-supplier conversion is likewise confined
  to manager initialization.
- **Rediscala #20075, non-actor paths:** immutable pool, cluster, master/replica, and Sentinel clients
  use the memoized `REQUEST_TARGET` path. Mutable pools retain a volatile immutable target in
  `MutablePoolState` and rebuild it only from synchronized snapshots after real pool mutations.
- **Peer PRs #20080, #20084, and #20086:** the added per-execution address work records the observed
  connection/socket peer, which is explicitly excluded. Their configured targets are inherited
  from #20077, #20073, and #20072 respectively and are reused.
- **Redisson atomic-batch #19204:** its logical batch request intentionally has no single configured
  target because a batch can span nodes. Its per-command state concerns batch aggregation and
  suppression, not configured-target construction.

## Uncertain cases excluded

- Lettuce standalone connection advice may run again while establishing a replacement connection.
  The inspected wiring creates and populates a new endpoint/connection carrier before initialization
  commands; it does not establish reconstruction on each command against one reusable carrier.
  This was treated as connection initialization, not a violation.
- Jedis `initializeSlotsCache`, Sentinel initialization, and provider initialization can rebuild
  aggregate targets. The inspected call sites are initialization or actual topology/failover
  changes. There was no evidence that they execute once per command with unchanged configuration.
- Rediscala's final `return of(client)` fallback was not reported separately. No concrete
  repeatedly instrumented, configured client was established that reaches it and produces a target;
  the definite direct-actor case is the earlier branch already reported.

## Search coverage

Repository guidance consulted: `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The requested
`.github/agents/knowledge/README.md` and articles could not be opened because this sandbox
explicitly prohibits access to `.github/agents`; no claim in this report relies on those files.

GitHub discovery searches:

```text
author:trask is:open redis
author:trask is:open Redis in:title
author:trask is:open Redisson in:title
author:trask is:open Valkey in:title
```

The broad search was supplemented with direct inspection of the problem's named PRs, stacked base
#20070, and older open Redisson batch PR #19204. Complete GitHub changed-file/diff payloads and exact
head files were inspected for all 14 code PRs listed above. Review threads were also fetched for
#20071, #20072, #20073, #20074, #20075, #20076, #20077, #20078, #20080, #20082, #20084, #20086,
and #19204.

Exact source searches across `main`, PR diffs, and heads included:

```text
RedisServerTarget
redisServerTarget
serverTarget
getServerTarget
RedisServerTarget.of
ofHostAndPort
ofEndpoint
ofEndpoints
ofUnorderedEndpoints
ofEndpointAndUnorderedEndpoints
ofUnorderedEndpointsAndLogicalName
endpoint(
capture
copy
withServerTarget
updateServerTarget
VirtualField
ThreadLocal
reconnect
dispatch
write
send
flush
subscribe
```

For `main`, production `RedisServerTarget` references were searched separately from tests, and all
Redis-family production source paths were enumerated. For each PR, target factories were traced
backward to configuration capture and forward through client/manager/pool/connection/request state
into command, batch, callback, transaction, and reactive execution paths. Copy/update helpers were
checked to distinguish a new target from reuse of an existing immutable reference.

Formatting, lint, build, and test commands were **skipped by design** because this was a read-only
source audit and the only repository change is this report.
